header.name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Tata Consultancy Services (NSE: TCS), part of the Tata Group, sells IT services and consulting; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹2,67,021 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹73,188 crore, 11.2% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 24.0% against 25.2%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹13,884 crore, 15.0% higher.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: The year-on-year comparison includes Coastal Cloud, which TCS acquired after the year-earlier quarter, so part of the revenue growth was bought rather than grown; the split is not separated here.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: A simple trend forecast this project made from earlier quarters had revenue within 0.5% of the actual but put the operating margin 1.49 percentage points too high; that forecast was not pre-registered, so its date cannot be proven.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 9 Oct 2026, the first session after the result, TCS shares rose 3.85% while the NIFTY 50 rose 1.30% and the NIFTY IT index rose 3.02%; allowing for the market's move, TCS's own move was +2.98%, about 1.75 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the IT sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹2,442 (NSE close, 12 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 10.76% cost of capital matches the price if revenue grows about 4.2% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 25.0%; TCS's revenue grew 8.6% a year over FY22–FY26.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: That four-year rate is lifted by FY23's 17.6%; the three years since grew 6.8%, 6.0% and 4.6%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹2,629 to ₹3,728 a share) and to how long TCS keeps earning high returns on new investment (anywhere from returns equal to its cost of capital to a quarter above its past level: a model value of ₹2,279 to ₹3,105 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next test of the mechanical forecast.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, less lease liabilities, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹46k crore of cash and treasury, which is why it looks so high.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY22–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY22 to FY26. FY23 alone grew 17.6%; the three years since grew less.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of TCS's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.what: Revenue grows only at FY26's pace for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY22-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and TCS keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at H1 FY27's year-on-year pace (which includes an acquisition) for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
The base growth anchor includes FY23's unusually large jump; later years grew more slowly.
Leases are the only debt; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.
The Q2 FY27 forecast was not pre-registered, so its timing cannot be proven. The next quarter will be.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
